statements.worth_reason: A new NVIDIA programme to rent back customers' unused GPUs at a fixed rate is a credit-support obligation that adds cash and credit risk and changes how neocloud demand should be read; core for the backstop-obligation question.
statements.day_note: Nvidia's post is undated in the article; original_day 2026-07-02 is the reporter's own statement day, and the adoption is a state as of that day, so the record is acceptable.

statements.worth_reason: Sizes what a first adopter is deploying under the backstop (170,000 GPUs), which bounds NVIDIA's potential rent-back exposure and is a sized demand datapoint.
statements.one_line_problem: Read alone it does not say Firmus is one of the first adopters of Nvidia's backstop, the reason the size matters here; that link sits only in e1 (the standard: a record must be understood on its own).

statements.worth_reason: Sizes the second named adopter's deployment under the backstop (40,000 GB300), same use as e2.
statements.one_line_problem: Same as e2: it does not say Sharon AI is a backstop adopter, so the record loses the condition that ties it to NVIDIA's obligation.

statements.worth_reason: NVIDIA's own terms: standard product revenue plus a share of cloud revenue on supported capacity, with credit support; this defines the economics and the risk of the new obligation.
statements.day_note: original_day correctly left unknown (the post is undated); event_time 2026-07-02 is only the report day.
statements.tier_note: fact: the item reports Nvidia's announcement of the programme (an announcement the item reports is a fact; the table's upper row wins), with the claims about adoption and earnings as secondary parts noted in the summary; e1 tiers the same announcement as fact.

statements.worth_reason: A restated September 2025 deal; as a prior backstop of the same kind it is the baseline for the size of NVIDIA's obligations, but it is old news to an analyst.
statements.one_line_problem: Does not say this was a backstop deal of the same kind ('deals like this'), so read alone the $6.3bn says nothing about the obligation it measures.

statements.worth_reason: A restated 2025 deal of the same kind; baseline for the obligation total, old news.
statements.one_line_problem: Says 'the item gives no signing date', but the article places the Lambda deal in 2025; and like e5 it drops that this was a backstop deal of the same kind.
statements.day_note: 2025: 'having previously done so with the likes of CoreWeave and Lambda in 2025'; the record leaves event_time blank.

questions.reason: It is the standard's own class-C example (NVIDIA's obligation to backstop cloud customers' capacity, read from the FY2027 annual report) and can change cash and credit risk; minor flaws: calling it 'financing' (measure financing_amount) mixes financing with a rent-back purchase commitment and credit support, and the 10-K may not break the programme out, so it may resolve as not determinable.

grade_reason: The main point, NVIDIA's new rent-back and revenue-share backstop for neoclouds with its first adopters, is captured (e1, e4) and the right class-C obligation question is opened. Defects are minor: sentence-by-sentence splitting strips context, so the Firmus, Sharon AI, CoreWeave and Lambda records do not say they are backstop deals; the Lambda record loses its 2025 date; Nvidia's announcement is tiered as a party statement in e4 but as a fact in e1.
standard_doubt: '重提的过去实际数可选；重提的季度指引和仍然有效的预测、计划按本来分量' (D243 item 6): a restated past obligation still in force (the CoreWeave $6.3bn backstop signed September 2025) fits both 'restated past actual' (optional) and 'plan still in force' (full weight); the standard does not say which, and for the backstop-obligation question it is exactly the baseline an analyst needs.
